title: How a Pile of Dirt Becomes a Castle
script: If you pile dirt into a hill and stand on top of it when the raiders come, you have a castle. But they just run up the hill and stab you, so you dig a ditch around it, throw that dirt on top to make it steeper, and ring the summit with a wall of sharpened logs. This is a motte. But wood burns, and one flaming arrow sets your whole wall on fire, so you tear it down and build a tower out of stone. This is a keep. But now they drag a battering ram up to your door, so you hang a heavy iron-tipped gate that drops from above, and you cut holes in the ceiling behind it to drop rocks and boiling water on anyone who gets through. These are murder holes. But the enemy stops attacking your walls and tunnels under them instead, propping the tunnel with wood and then burning the props. In 1215, King John brought down a corner of Rochester Castle with the fat of forty pigs, so you build round towers, because a round tower has no corner to dig under. That is why castle towers are round. But ladders still reach your wall, and you can't hit anyone at the bottom without leaning out, so you build stone walkways that hang over the edge, with holes in the floor. But one breach and you've lost everything, so you build a second, taller wall inside the first, and your archers shoot right over it. This is a concentric castle. Add a moat, arrow slits, and a drawbridge. Congratulations, you have built a castle.
